items.title: Constitutional Bodies — Overview & Distinction
items.body:
## What makes a body 'constitutional'

- **Constitutional bodies** derive their authority **directly from the Constitution**, which makes them autonomous and independent of the executive and legislature.
- Contrast three categories a candidate must never confuse:

| Type | Basis of creation | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Constitutional** | Named/created by the Constitution | ECI (324), UPSC/SPSC (315-323), CAG (148), Finance Commission (280), NCSC (338), NCST (338A), NCBC (338B), Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B), GST Council (279A), Attorney General (76), Advocate General (165) |
| **Statutory** | Act of Parliament | NHRC, CIC, Lokpal, CVC, NCW |
| **Executive** | Cabinet resolution | NITI Aayog (2015) |

- Their importance: **independence and autonomy**, **checks and balances** on the executive/legislature, **accountability and transparency**, and **upholding democracy**.
keyPoints: Constitutional bodies derive authority directly from the Constitution; they are autonomous and independent.
NITI Aayog (executive, 2015) and NHRC/CIC/Lokpal (statutory) are NOT constitutional bodies.
Key articles: ECI 324, UPSC/SPSC 315-323, CAG 148, Finance Commission 280, Inter-State Council 263.
Social-justice commissions: NCSC 338, NCST 338A, NCBC 338B; Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities 350B.
GST Council is under Article 279A; Attorney General 76 and Advocate General 165 are law officers.
items.mnemonic: Constitutional = written into the Constitution; Statutory = written into a statute; Executive = a Cabinet note.

items.title: Election Commission of India (Article 324)
items.body:
## Composition & evolution

- **Article 324** vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to **Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President** in the ECI.
- Established **1950** as a **single-member** body; two ECs added in **1989**, abolished January **1990**, and permanently **multi-member (three members)** since **October 1993**.
- The **President** appoints the CEC and other ECs; the CEC is the chairman. Disputes among them are decided **by majority**.

## Tenure, removal & independence

- Term: **6 years or up to age 65**, whichever is earlier.
- The **CEC** is removed only in the **same manner as a Supreme Court judge**; an **EC or Regional Commissioner** can be removed **only on the CEC's recommendation** — the asymmetry that protects the CEC.
- Service conditions of the CEC cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.

## Key powers

- Delimit constituencies (under the Delimitation Commission Act), prepare/revise electoral rolls, notify schedules, scrutinise nominations.
- Grant recognition to parties and allot symbols; act as a court for such disputes.
- Frame and enforce the **Model Code of Conduct**; advise the President/Governor on disqualification of legislators; register parties as national/state.
keyPoints: Article 324 covers Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President — NOT local bodies.
ECI was single-member until 1989 and permanently multi-member (3 members) from October 1993.
CEC removed like a Supreme Court judge; an EC/Regional Commissioner only on the CEC's recommendation.
Term of CEC/ECs: 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier; salary equal to a Supreme Court judge.
ECI registers parties, allots symbols, and enforces the Model Code of Conduct; State-level help from the Chief Electoral Officer.

items.title: UPSC & SPSC (Articles 315-323)
items.body:
## Union Public Service Commission

- Central recruiting agency; **Articles 315-323 (Part XIV)** govern composition, appointment, removal, powers and independence.
- Usually **9-11 members** appointed by the **President**; the only condition — about **half** must have held office for **at least 10 years** under the Union or a State. Term: **6 years or age 65**.
- **Removal**: by the President for insolvency, paid outside employment, or infirmity; for **misbehaviour**, only after a **Supreme Court inquiry whose advice is binding**.
- **Independence**: expenses charged on the **Consolidated Fund of India**; service conditions cannot be varied adversely; the **chairman is barred from any further government employment**.
- **Functions advisory only** — recruitment to All-India/Central Services (Groups A & B) and disciplinary matters. Failure to consult gives **no court remedy**. The President may exclude posts, but such regulations lie before Parliament for **14 days**.

## State Public Service Commission — the contrasts

| Feature | UPSC | SPSC |
|---|---|---|
| Appointed by | President | **Governor** |
| Age limit | 65 | **62** |
| Removed by | President | **President only** (not Governor) |

- A **Joint SPSC** for two or more states is a **statutory** body (created by Parliament), not constitutional.
keyPoints: UPSC: Articles 315-323; usually 9-11 members appointed by the President; term 6 years or age 65.
About half the members must have held office 10 years under the Union or a State — the only constitutional condition.
UPSC recommendations are advisory; failure to consult gives no judicial remedy; expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
SPSC members are appointed by the Governor (age limit 62) but can be removed only by the President.
A Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) is a statutory, not a constitutional, body.
items.mnemonic: Governor gives the SPSC job (62), but only the President can take it away.

items.title: CAG (Art 148) & Finance Commission (Art 280)
items.body:
## Comptroller and Auditor General

- **Article 148**; head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, **guardian of the public purse**; appointed by the **President** by warrant.
- Term **6 years or age 65**; removed **only like a Supreme Court judge**; **not eligible for further office** after demitting.
- **Duties (Art 149-151)**: audits the Consolidated Fund of the Union, States and UTs with a legislature, the Contingency Fund and Public Account; submits **three reports** (Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, Public Undertakings) examined by the **Public Accounts Committee**.
- **India vs Britain**: India's CAG is **only Auditor General** — audits **after** spending, with **no control over the issue of money**; Britain's is **both Comptroller and Auditor General**, so money there can be drawn only with his approval.

## Finance Commission

- **Article 280**; constituted by the President **every fifth year** (or earlier); a **chairman + 4 members**, all **reappointable**.
- Recommends **tax devolution** between Centre and States, **grants-in-aid**, and measures to augment State funds for **panchayats/municipalities**.
- Recommendations are **advisory** only.
- **16th Finance Commission**: chaired by **Arvind Panagariya** (award period from 2026-27).
keyPoints: CAG (Article 148): term 6 years/age 65; removed only like a Supreme Court judge; ineligible for further office.
CAG audits after expenditure and has no control over the issue of money — unlike Britain's CAG (both Comptroller and Auditor).
CAG submits three reports (Appropriation, Finance, Public Undertakings); acts as guide to the Public Accounts Committee.
Finance Commission (Article 280): constituted every fifth year; chairman + 4 members; recommendations advisory.
The 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya, covering the award period from 2026-27.

items.title: Social-Justice Commissions & Law Officers
items.body:
## NCSC, NCST & NCBC

- Originally **Article 338** provided a single **Special Officer for SCs and STs**. The **89th Amendment, 2003** created the separate **NCSC (Art 338)** and **NCST (Art 338A)**.
- Each = **chairperson + vice-chairperson + 3 members** appointed by the President; each has the **powers of a civil court** (summoning, requiring documents, receiving affidavits).
- **NCBC** became constitutional via the **102nd Amendment, 2018 (Article 338B)** — earlier a statutory body (NCBC Act, 1993). The amendment also added **Article 342A** (President specifies SEBCs) and amended Article 366; **Article 340** underlies commissions on backward classes (Kaka Kalelkar 1953, Mandal 1979; Indra Sawhney 1992).

## Attorney General & Advocate General

| Feature | Attorney General (Art 76) | Advocate General (Art 165) |
|---|---|---|
| Appointed by | President | Governor |
| Qualification | Qualified as **Supreme Court** judge | Qualified as **High Court** judge |
| Tenure | Pleasure of the President | Pleasure of the Governor |
| Privilege | Speak in Parliament, **no vote** | Speak in State legislature, **no vote** |

- The AG is the **highest law officer**; may do private practice but not against the Government; the **Solicitor General** is a statutory office **not mentioned in Article 76**.

## Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

- **Article 350B**, inserted by the **7th Amendment, 1956** on the **States Reorganisation Commission's** recommendation; investigates safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President.
keyPoints: 89th Amendment (2003) split the SC/ST body into NCSC (Art 338) and NCST (Art 338A); each has civil-court powers.
NCBC gained constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment, 2018 (Article 338B); Article 342A lets the President specify SEBCs.
Attorney General (Art 76): appointed by President, qualified as SC judge, holds office at President's pleasure.
Advocate General (Art 165): appointed by Governor, qualified as HC judge — the State's highest law officer.
Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art 350B) added by the 7th Amendment, 1956 on the States Reorganisation Commission's advice.

items.title: GST Council & Current Office-Holders (Sep 2026)
items.body:
## GST Council (Article 279A)

- Created by the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act** (GST rolled out 1 July 2017); a federal, cooperative-federalism body.
- **Chaired ex-officio by the Union Finance Minister**; members include the Union Minister of State for Finance and each State's Finance/Taxation Minister.
- **Voting**: the **Centre = one-third** and **all States together = two-thirds** of the votes; every decision needs a **three-fourths weighted majority** of members present and voting.

## Current office-holders (verified online, September 2026)

| Office | Article | Holder |
|---|---|---|
| Chief Election Commissioner (26th) | 324 | **Gyanesh Kumar** (since 19 Feb 2025) |
| Comptroller & Auditor General (15th) | 148 | **K. Sanjay Murthy** (since 21 Nov 2024) |
| Attorney General of India (16th) | 76 | **R. Venkataramani** (since 1 Oct 2022) |
| Chairman, UPSC | 316 | **Ajay Kumar** (IAS) |
| Chairman, 16th Finance Commission | 280 | **Arvind Panagariya** |
| Chair, GST Council (ex-officio) | 279A | **Nirmala Sitharaman** (Union FM) |
| Chairman, NCSC | 338 | **Kishor Makwana** |
| Chairman, NCST | 338A | **Antar Singh Arya** |
| Chairman, NCBC | 338B | **Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti** |

- **APPSC** (State PSC for Andhra Pradesh): headquartered at **Vijayawada**, sanctioned strength **Chairman + 9 members**.
keyPoints: GST Council (Article 279A) created by the 101st Amendment; chaired ex-officio by the Union Finance Minister.
GST Council voting: Centre one-third, States two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority.
As of Sep 2026: CEC Gyanesh Kumar; CAG K. Sanjay Murthy; Attorney General R. Venkataramani; UPSC Chairman Ajay Kumar.
16th Finance Commission Chairman Arvind Panagariya; GST Council chair Nirmala Sitharaman (Union FM).
NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana, NCST Chairman Antar Singh Arya, NCBC Chairman Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti; APPSC HQ Vijayawada (Chairman + 9 members).

items.title: Andhra Pradesh Constitutional & Statutory Authorities (2026)
items.body:
## APPSC (Articles 315-323)

- State Public Service Commission for AP; **Governor appoints** Chairman & members; **removal only by the President** (Art 317) — protecting independence. **HQ: Vijayawada**. Present Chairman (as of Sep 2026): **Prof. C. Sashidhar (Full Additional Charge)**.

## Constitutional bodies for local government

| Body | Provision | Appointed/constituted by | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **State Election Commission** | Art 243K / 243ZA | Governor (State Election Commissioner) | Panchayat & municipal elections |
| **State Finance Commission** | Art 243-I / 243-Y | Governor, every 5 years | Devolution/grants to local bodies |

> Note: **ECI (Art 324)**, not the SEC, conducts Assembly/Council & Parliament elections.

## Statutory watchdog & rights bodies

- **Lokayukta & Upa-Lokayukta** — under the **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983** (statutory anti-corruption ombudsman; Maharashtra was first, 1971).
- **AP State Human Rights Commission** — under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**.
- **AP State Commission for Women** — statutory women's-welfare body.

(All three are **statutory**, not constitutional, bodies.)
keyPoints: APPSC under Arts 315-323; Governor appoints, President removes (Art 317); HQ Vijayawada; Chairman Prof. C. Sashidhar (FAC, Sep 2026)
AP State Election Commission (Art 243K/243ZA) runs local-body polls; ECI runs Assembly/Parliament polls
AP State Finance Commission constituted by Governor every 5 years (Arts 243-I & 243-Y)
AP Lokayukta & Upa-Lokayukta = statutory ombudsman under the AP Lokayukta Act, 1983
AP SHRC (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993) and AP Women's Commission are statutory, not constitutional, bodies
items.source: Constitution (Arts 243, 315-323) / official AP bodies; APPSC chair verified via Wikipedia as of Sep 2026

items.title: PYQ Precision — PAC, NDC & Presidential Election
items.body:
## Public Accounts Committee (PAC)

- **22 members** = **15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha**; **1-year** term; a **minister cannot** be a member.
- Chairperson is, **by convention (since 1967), from the Opposition**.
- Examines the **CAG's** audit reports (Appropriation & Finance Accounts); the CAG is its 'friend, philosopher and guide'.

## National Development Council (NDC)

- **Extra-constitutional, non-statutory** body (executive resolution, 1952) — **not** in the Constitution.
- Members: **PM (head) + all Union Cabinet Ministers + CMs of all States + UT administrators + NITI Aayog members**.
- The **Finance Commission Chairman is NOT** a member (common trap).

## Election of the President — value of votes

- **MLA vote value = (State 1971 population ÷ total elected MLAs) ÷ 1000** → **varies State to State**.
- **Every MP** (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) has the **same** vote value; total MPs' value ≈ total MLAs' value (**Union–State parity**).
- Method: proportional representation, single transferable vote, secret ballot.
keyPoints: PAC = 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha); 1-year term; chair from Opposition by convention; examines CAG reports.
A minister cannot be a member of the PAC.
NDC is extra-constitutional/non-statutory (1952); NOT mentioned in the Constitution.
NDC members: PM + all Union Cabinet Ministers + all CMs + UT administrators + NITI Aayog; the Finance Commission Chairman is NOT a member.
President's election: each MLA's vote value varies by State; every MP has equal vote value (Union-State parity).
items.source: UPSC 2013 & 2018 Prelims (Rau's IAS COMPASS); Constitution Arts 54-55, 280
